newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate shoots up to 9.1 vs 7.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate shoots up to 9.1 vs 7.6 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate shot back up to 9.1 percent on Wednesday from 7.6 percent, propelled by term loans at higher rates despite weaker demand.
Dealers said new interbank demand was met in total at an unchanged rate of 8.0 percent for call money, while 10-15 day funds were granted at 12 percent.
Insurers rolled over five-10 day placements at a steady 7.0 percent. One-month bank loans fetched 12 percent.
Trade shrank to 14.4 million kuna against supply of 25 million as dealers said banks' accounts were still thin.
But they said four borrowers squared their Tuesday's overnight shortfalls of 6.6 million kuna without any problem.
The central bank calculated kuna midrates for Thursday firmer at 5.4293 and 3.5618 to the dollar and mark, respectively. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
